subject: SLA & Premium Care — response matrices and quote
body:
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: lisa.gomez@acmeretail.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA & Premium Care — response matrices and quote

Hi Lisa,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is a short proposal for Redwood Premium Care (SLA + escalation coverage) and a response matrix to map severity to response/engagement timelines. High level summary below — I tried to keep things modular so you can pick the coverage you want without overcommitting.

Offer (monthly, list price):
- Standard Care: 99.9% uptime target, business-hours (M-F 9am–6pm PT) email support, P1 response < 60 mins, P2 < 4 hours — $3,500/month
- Premium Care: 99.95% uptime target, extended-hours (M-F 8am–8pm PT) phone + email, P1 response < 30 mins, P2 < 2 hours — $8,000/month
- Critical Care (recommended for production-critical workloads): 99.99% uptime target, 24x7 on-call rota, guaranteed on-call callback for P1 within 15 mins, named L2 escalation engineer during business hours — $18,500/month

Bulk discounts (applies to total monthly fee with a 12/24 month commit):
- 12-month term = 15% off list monthly
- 24-month term = 25% off list monthly

SLA credits: credits are pro-rated by downtime minutes beyond the uptime target; we calculate at the invoice period level and cap credits at one month of recurring fees per 12-month period. Critical incident definition: events causing platform-wide or customer-impacting sustained failures to inference or control plane (see attached PDF for exact legal language).

Attachments: Redwood_Premium_Care_2025.pdf (full terms + sample amendment), escalation_matrix.xlsx (response matrix by severity)

Next steps: if you can confirm (a) target uptime tier, (b) preferred contract term (12 vs 24 months), and (c) whether you want the named L2 during business hours included, I can return a final quote and a DocuSign-ready amendment by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

-----Original Message-----
From: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@acmeretail.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 12:45:22 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA & Premium Care — response matrices and quote

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the detailed breakdown — this is helpful. A couple of questions before I run this past procurement and legal:
1) Can you clarify the exact definition of "Critical incident" you use to calculate credits? Our legal team will want precise triggers.
2) Do credits reduce our invoice immediately or are they applied to the next invoice?
3) If we agree to a 12-month term at 15% off, can we get the named L2 engineer during business hours included without moving to Critical Care? We're trying to avoid the full Critical Care price but want faster engagement for P1s.
4) Will an SLA downgrade/fallback (e.g., temporary failover to a lower-tier model) be considered a creditable event?

CC'ing our procurement lead legal@acmeretail.com.

Thanks,
Lisa Gomez
Head of Infrastructure | Acme Retail
lisa.gomez@acmeretail.com

On Tue, Sep 16, 2025 at 08:30 AM -0700, rafael_mendes@redwood.com wrote:

Hi Lisa — quick answers inline and a proposal to keep the commitment and price you asked about.

1) Critical incident: operational definition in the attached PDF (short): "a sustained customer-impacting failure of inference requests or control-plane operations preventing normal service for more than 5 consecutive minutes and affecting >= 5% of requests or an externally visible outage identified in customer monitoring." We can add specific thresholds into the contract for Acme if needed (i.e., lower the percent threshold).

2) Credits: applied as invoice credits on the next invoice cycle; can be used to offset charges within the same 30-day window.

3) Named L2: we can include a named L2 escalation engineer as an add-on to Premium Care for a flat $3,500/month (dedicated during business hours). If you take a 12-month term we can include that L2 for the first 6 months at no additional charge as part of the 15% discount bundle — effectively trialing the named coverage. If you'd like it permanently bundled we can roll it into a custom Critical-lite package and price it accordingly.

4) SLA downgrade/fallbacks: planned, documented failovers (e.g., temporary traffic routing to a lower-tier model during capacity constraints) are not automatically eligible for credits. Unexpected failovers that result from Redwood service failures would be assessed case-by-case and can be creditable. We'll add a clause to the amendment to make this explicit.

Proposed concrete path:
- 12-month term, Premium Care
- 15% discount applied to monthly fees
- Named L2 included for first 6 months at no extra charge
- Finalized amendment with clarified definitions and credit flow (DocuSign link provided once you confirm)

I'll draft the amendment and loop in legal and Neha for final review.

Cheers,
Rafael

On Wed, Sep 17, 2025 10:02:11 -0700, marissa_cole@redwood.com wrote:

Rafael / Lisa — adding the escalation playbook detail from our ops team. For clarity around P1 engagement timelines we recommend the following as operational SLAs (these are the times our on-call and escalation engineers will target for initial contact and remediation steps):
- P1 (Critical): initial contact from on-call within 15 minutes, follow-up every 30 minutes until ETA provided; remediation handoff to named L2 within 60 minutes for complex failures requiring infra-side fix.
- P2 (High): initial contact within 2 hours, remediation plan within 8 business hours.
- P3 (Normal): response within 24 business hours.

Also — escalation_matrix.xlsx contains the contact tree (primary on-call, secondary, named L2 contact details) and example runbooks for common issues (model OOMs, KV cache corruption, degraded throughput). If Acme wants the named L2 to be on a dedicated pager list, we need to confirm working hours and acceptable on-call rotation.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

-----Original Message-----
From: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@acmeretail.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acmeretail.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 15:18:04 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA & Premium Care — response matrices and quote

Rafael / Marissa — thanks, both. Procurement will sign for the 12-month term at 15% off. We want the named L2 included for the first 6 months as proposed. A few legal items to close before we sign:
- Please include the exact incident thresholds in the amendment (we'll expect the 5-minute sustained window and the >=5% request impact as a starting point).
- Credits should be applied to the next invoice and clearly itemized.
- Confirm that planned failover (we route traffic to a backup model to preserve latency) will not trigger credits, but unplanned Redwood service failures will.

If you can send a final amendment with these items and a DocuSign link, procurement will route for signature. We aim to have the signed amendment by next Wednesday.

Thanks — Lisa
